items.item:
12. Two concurrent creates with one request id and equal facts — of a
    project, a Customer, a room of one project, a pointer of one project by
    one publisher (for Kernel, naming one session) — make one record; the
    other answers it. With different facts, or another publisher, the second
    is refused as a conflict. The same request id for rooms of two different
    projects makes two rooms.
   Shows A01-1, A01-3, A01-4. [witness: verification:registry_a01_concurrent_creates_make_one_record]
statements:
```text
for each model m in {Project, Customer}, and per project for m in   -- A01-1
{Room, ArtifactPointer}:
  for records r1 != r2 of m with r1.request_id and r2.request_id present:
    r1.request_id != r2.request_id
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f) where existing r of m has r.request_id = k:
  a check of stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 fails, or m in   -- A01-2
  {Room, ArtifactPointer} with its project archived => refused, store unchanged
  otherwise, f = current_facts(r)  => answer r, store unchanged   -- A01-3
  otherwise, f != current_facts(r) => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-4
```

quotes: assert sorted(answer["changed"] for answer in answers) == [False, True], answers
verdicts.why: The check detects one creation plus one unchanged answer for equal concurrent project, customer, room, and pointer calls; detects conflicts for differing project/customer/room facts and publishers; and verifies that the same room request id is scoped per project. It does not test differing pointer contents from the same publisher, and for the concurrent equal-fact and different-fact cases it does not snapshot the whole store, so the A01-3/A01-4 requirement that the repeat or refusal leave the store unchanged is only weakly covered; the explicit store comparison applies only to the later different-session publisher conflict.
